newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Duma wants Yeltsin to drop Chubais temporarily.
newsitem.headline: Duma wants Yeltsin to drop Chubais temporarily.

text.p: Russia's opposition-led lower house of parliament urged President Boris Yeltsin on Friday to temporarily relieve Kremlin chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais of his duties because of his alleged role in a political scandal.

The State Duma approved a non-binding appeal urging Yeltsin to drop Chubais until the scandal, over alleged financial irregularities during the president's re-election campaign last summer, is cleared up.
The Duma also urged Yeltsin to relieve first deputy prime minister Viktor Ilyushin, a former presidential adviser, of his duties temporarily. Ilyushin and Chubais deny any wrongdoing.

"The State Duma turns to you, esteemed Boris Nikolayevich, with a proposal that you look into the question of the disciplinary responsibility of V.V. Ilyushin and A.B. Chubais and relieve them of their duties until this question is settled," said the Duma appeal.
It was adopted by 263 votes to none. One deputy abstained and 186 members of the 450-seat house did not attend.

State prosecutors say they will investigate the scandal, which erupted last week when the Moskovsky Komsomolets newspaper published the transcript of a bugged conversation which it said Ilyushin, Chubais and another official had on June 22.

The transcript portrayed Chubais and Ilyushin as conspiring to block an investigation by prosecutors into the detention of two of their campaign staff allegedly caught leaving the government building with half a million dollars in cash.

At the time all those involved in the incident, which took place between rounds one and two of the presidential election, denied that the two men were carrying the money and insisted they were framed by political rivals.

Chubais, who says the transcript is a forgery, said on Friday he wanted the truth to come out. "I am ready to answer all questions," the 41-year-old former privatisation guru told Interfax news agency.

The communists who dominate Russia's Duma loathe Chubais and his market reforms and have accused him of amassing power during Yeltsin's prolonged absence from the Kremlin culminating in heart surgery in early November.

Yeltsin, who often ignores the Duma's demands, met Chubais at the Barvikha sanatorium outside Moscow after leaving the capital's Central Clinical Hospital on Friday morning. Details of their talks were not immediately available.
